name: Hexapeptide-11

card.summary: A six-amino-acid peptide originally isolated from yeast, used in skincare for firmness and to protect skin cells from ageing stress.
card.note: Evidence is mostly cell-culture work from the ingredient's developers.

quick.overview:
Hexapeptide-11 is a peptide with the sequence Phe-Val-Ala-Pro-Phe-Pro, first found in yeast extracts and made synthetically for cosmetics. It is marketed for skin firmness and for slowing signs of cellular ageing.

In lab work on human skin and lung fibroblasts it switched on protective pathways and protected cells from oxidative stress; one paper also reported improved skin elasticity in human subjects.
quick.how: It is an ingredient in serums and creams applied to the skin, usually alongside other peptides and hydrating ingredients. Studies used it in concentrations of about 0.1 to 1 percent in cell cultures. Users apply it as part of a normal routine.
quick.risks: The cell studies found no significant toxicity in normal human fibroblasts. As a topical cosmetic peptide it has little published human safety data beyond that.

lead: Hexapeptide-11 (Peptamide-6) is a synthetic peptide of structure FVAPFP, originally isolated from yeast extracts and later made by solid-phase synthesis. [1][2]

It is used in anti-ageing skincare to improve firmness. Researchers report it reversibly lowers ATM and p53 expression, which control entry into cellular senescence, in aged fibroblasts and dermal papilla cells in vitro. [1]

A 2015 paper found it activated proteasome, autophagy, chaperone and antioxidant genes, protected fibroblasts from oxidative-stress-induced senescence, and improved skin elasticity in skin-deformation assays in human subjects. [2]

chain: Peptide applied in a topical product
Cell studies show protective and anti-senescence pathways activated
angle.text: It is applied to skin in creams and serums for firmness. Developer-linked studies report better elasticity measurements and fibroblast protection from oxidative stress.

paras: The peptide was isolated from yeast extracts and made by solid-state synthesis to high purity. [1][2]
It is reported to lower ATM and p53 expression, with effects at 0.1 to 1.0 percent in two cell types, and to activate Nrf2 and proteostasis pathways. [1][2]

A 2015 Redox Biology study found no significant toxicity in normal human lung or skin fibroblasts, protection against premature senescence, and improved elasticity in in-vivo skin deformation tests in human subjects. [2] A 2013 study reported in-vitro senescence modulation. [1] A 2021 study tested five cosmeceutical peptides in mixtures against peroxide-induced senescence in skin fibroblasts. [3] No large randomised trials of facial appearance were found.
